items.prompt: What does the term 'marine mammal' refer to?

options.label: Mammals that rely on marine ecosystems for their existence
options.feedback: That's correct. Marine mammals are mammals that depend on marine environments for feeding and survival.

options.label: Mammals that live only in freshwater
options.feedback: Freshwater is not the same as marine. Marine mammals rely on oceans or seas, though some, like river dolphins, live in rivers that connect to the sea.

options.label: Mammals that live only on land
options.feedback: Land mammals do not rely on marine environments. Marine mammals depend on the ocean for their existence.

options.label: Mammals that can fly over the ocean
options.feedback: Flying mammals like bats are not typically called marine mammals, even if some bats hunt over water. The term refers to mammals that depend on marine ecosystems.

items.ok_line: Marine mammals depend on the sea to live and feed.
items.ko_line: Marine mammals are tied to oceans, not to land or freshwater.
items.exp_text: Marine mammals are an informal group of mammals whose survival depends entirely or almost entirely on the oceans. They include cetaceans, pinnipeds, sirenians, sea otters, and polar bears, and they feed in marine environments.

items.prompt: Which animals are fully aquatic marine mammals?

options.label: Seals and sea lions
options.feedback: Seals and sea lions are pinnipeds, which are semiaquatic—they spend most time in water but return to land to mate and molt.

options.label: Polar bears
options.feedback: Polar bears are mostly terrestrial and go into water only when necessary, so they are not fully aquatic.

options.label: Sea otters
options.feedback: Sea otters live in kelp forests and estuaries, but they are not fully aquatic like cetaceans and sirenians; they still come to land sometimes.

options.label: Whales and manatees
options.feedback: Correct. Both cetaceans (whales, dolphins, porpoises) and sirenians (manatees, dugongs) are fully aquatic and depend on water for all stages of life.

items.ok_line: Cetaceans and sirenians never leave the water.
items.ko_line: Pinnipeds, polar bears, and sea otters are not obligate water dwellers.
items.exp_text: Cetaceans and sirenians are fully aquatic, meaning they spend their entire lives in water. Pinnipeds are semiaquatic because they need land for breeding and molting, while polar bears are mostly terrestrial.

items.prompt: What do pinnipeds need to come to land for?

options.label: Feeding
options.feedback: Pinnipeds feed in the water, not on land. They come ashore for other vital activities.

options.label: Mating, breeding, and molting
options.feedback: Correct. Pinnipeds spend most of their time in water but must return to land or ice for mating, giving birth, and shedding their fur.

options.label: Drinking freshwater
options.feedback: Pinnipeds get water from their food and do not need to come ashore to drink.

options.label: Sleeping
options.feedback: Pinnipeds can sleep in water, so they do not need to come to land for that.

items.ok_line: Pinnipeds come ashore to mate, breed, and molt.
items.ko_line: Feeding and sleeping can happen in the water for pinnipeds.
items.exp_text: Pinnipeds are semiaquatic: they are well adapted to water but must haul out on land or ice for reproduction and molting. Their feeding happens in the ocean.

items.prompt: Which group of marine mammals is considered fully aquatic?

options.label: Cetaceans and sirenians
options.feedback: Correct. Both cetaceans (whales, dolphins) and sirenians (manatees, dugongs) are fully aquatic and never leave the water.

options.label: Pinnipeds
options.feedback: Pinnipeds are semiaquatic; they need land for mating and molting, so they are not fully aquatic.

options.label: Sea otters
options.feedback: Sea otters are not fully aquatic; they come to land and live in kelp forests and estuaries.

options.label: Polar bears
options.feedback: Polar bears are mostly terrestrial and enter water only when necessary, so they are not fully aquatic.

items.ok_line: Cetaceans and sirenians live only in water.
items.ko_line: Pinnipeds, otters, and bears are not obligate water dwellers.
items.exp_text: Cetaceans and sirenians are obligate water dwellers, meaning they cannot survive on land. Other marine mammals like pinnipeds and polar bears have varying degrees of land use.

options.label: A mammal that lives only in the ocean
options.feedback: That describes fully aquatic marine mammals, not quasi-marine ones. Quasi-marine mammals have great dependency on the sea but are not anatomically specialized.

options.label: A mammal that has flippers and a tail
options.feedback: Flippers are a sign of anatomical specialization, which quasi-marine mammals lack. They are not necessarily adapted with flippers.

options.label: A mammal that eats only marine plants
options.feedback: Diet is not the defining feature. Quasi-marine mammals rely on the sea but are not specialized for aquatic life.

options.label: A mammal that depends heavily on the sea but is not anatomically specialized for it
options.feedback: Correct. Quasi-marine mammals, like the arctic fox or fish-eating bats, rely on marine resources but have not evolved specialized aquatic traits.

items.ok_line: They depend on the sea without being specialized.
items.ko_line: Fully aquatic or specialized mammals are not quasi-marine.
items.exp_text: Quasi-marine mammals are those that have a strong reliance on the sea for food or survival but have not developed anatomical adaptations like flippers or blubber. Examples include the arctic fox and certain bats.
